terms.meaning: A named setting stored outside the code that a program reads when it starts.
A plain text file of name and value settings that the app loads at startup.
A human-readable text format often used for settings files.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and loading the settings file
sections.what: Brings in the file path, YAML, and .env reading tools, then reads the .env file so its values become available to the program.
sections.why: Likely reason: settings must be loaded before other modules read them.
sections.watch_out: Loading happens when this file is first imported, so any module that reads environment variables before this import will not see the .env values.

sections.name: Config (part 1)
sections.title: Loading settings from file and environment
sections.what: Reads the settings file config/config.yaml once when the program starts, then replaces some values with environment variables such as the database address, AI keys, and log level.
sections.why: Lets secrets and machine-specific values come from the environment instead of being stored in the file.
sections.watch_out: If a section such as llm or logging is missing from the YAML file, startup fails with a key error.

sections.name: Config: get
sections.title: Looking up a setting by name
sections.what: Lets other code ask for a setting using a dotted name, such as one for the AI model, and returns a default value if the setting is missing.
sections.why: Gives a simple way to read nested settings without repeating dictionary lookups.
sections.watch_out: A missing or misspelled setting name returns the default silently, so typos are not reported.

sections.name: Config: llm_model
sections.title: Choosing the AI model name
sections.what: Returns the model name for the chosen AI provider, either OpenAI or Anthropic, and uses a built-in name if none is set.
sections.why: Lets the app switch providers by changing one setting.
sections.watch_out: The built-in fallback model names are hardcoded and may not match the models you intend to use, and an unknown provider returns an empty name.

summary: Loads the .env settings file when the program starts. Only the loading step is visible in this packet; the shared settings object and its methods are not shown.
purpose: Makes settings available to the whole app from one place.
why: Likely reason: loading the settings file early means every later module sees the values.
how: Imports the file path, YAML, and .env reading tools, then loads .env when this file is first imported. The rest of the settings logic is not visible in this packet.
inputs: The .env file in the working folder and any environment variables already set.
outputs: Environment variables set for the program, plus a shared config object used by other modules.
risks: The .env file is found from the folder the program is started in, so starting from another folder silently ignores it. Variables already set on the computer may take priority over the file, depending on the loader's default behaviour. Most of the config logic was not reviewed.
debug: If a setting seems ignored, check the folder the program was started from and whether the same variable is set on the computer. Look for the settings value in the place the app reads it.
